text:
maya: heads up — we're seeing p95->p99 regression on hosted text-gen around 08:12 UTC, coincides with a bunch of CUDA OOMs on a few nodes. Customers filing latency tickets.
liam: which model/pool? any correlation to traffic shape?
jay: (on call) seeing same, adding notes here.
maya: model=redwood-v2-large, pool=dedicated-gpu-64, spike at 08:12. p95 ~120ms -> 320ms, p99 ~450ms -> 1.2s. logs show OOM+retry churn. sample log:
```
2026-03-15T08:12:07Z worker-23 ERR cuda: out of memory when allocating 1.20 GiB (total 40.0 GiB)
2026-03-15T08:12:07Z worker-23 WARN falling back to spill -> increased cpu path latency
2026-03-15T08:12:07Z worker-23 INFO kv_eviction: evicted 128MB from prefix cache
```
jen: looks like KV cache growth + fragmentation. we had a long chat campaign (lots of long chats with 32k context) from a single customer earlier.
liam: can we repro locally?
maya: repro steps I used:
1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: test-gpu-oom-01" -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large","input":"'$(python -c "print('A'*20000)")'","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
2) flood 4 concurrent requests per GPU for ~60s
Observed: memory reserved climbs, fragmentation ratio increases, eventually OOM then fallback -> CPU > latency.
alex: sharing a quick nvidia-smi snapshot from affected node:
```
Tue Mar 15 08:13:11 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. |
|  0  A100-SXM4-40GB     On     | 00000000:00:1E.0 Off |                  |
| 40GiB / 40GiB | 98% | Default |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0421 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0421) :rotating_light:
sre-oncall: thanks, ops-bot. immediate mitigation options:
- lower per-request max_context_tokens to 2048 for affected pool via route override
- temporarily route heavy-context customers to deduped/quantized variant (v2-large-8bit)
- set tenant-level KV cap (REDWOOD_KV_MAX_BYTES=200000000)
maya: did a quick config change to cap KV for that tenant, latency dropped back toward baseline within 2 mins.
liam: nice. we still need long-term fix — fragmentation suggests allocator behavior. alex any thoughts on allocator/env tweaks?
alex: yes — for PyTorch CUDA allocator we can set env: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
that reduces fragmentation by avoiding lots of tiny free blocks. also consider enabling `torch.cuda.memory_stats()` on suspect workers and expose `cuda_fragmentation_ratio` metric.
jen: also the KV cache implementation appends many small tensors over time — we should consider coalescing or switching to chunked allocations for cached KV blocks.
maya: metrics I pulled (PromQL):
- avg_over_time(gpu_free_bytes[5m]) shows a step down starting 08:10
- max_over_time(kv_cache_size_bytes{pool="dedicated-gpu-64"}[10m]) -> +3.2GB
- increase in export: gpu_fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 for ~7min
liam: can we add an alert: gpu_fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 for 5m AND gpu_free_bytes < threshold -> page oncall?
sre-oncall: yes, create a pager for that. also auto-drain nodes that report fragmentation>0.65 and OOMs>3 in 10m.
jen: interim software mitigations:
- trim the prefix KV at request end for chats older than N tokens
- enable periodic `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` after eviction windows (careful: can spike latency)
- reduce batch size floor (we were auto-batching to 8 when memory tight; drop to 4)
alex: infra mitigation: schedule a rolling restart of worker processes every 6h to avoid long-term fragmentation growth. expensive but reduces OOM tail.
maya: repro artifact attached to the ticket: request dump, `nvidia-smi` traces, `pytorch memory snapshot` (snapshots show reserved vs allocated mismatch).
liam: action items:
- ENG-RUNTIME: implement metric export for cuda_fragmentation_ratio + kv_cache_size_bytes (owner: alex)
- ENG-ML: evaluate KV coalescing and memory footprint reduction (owner: jen)
- SRE: alert + runbook for fragmentation-induced p99 regressions + temporary route rules (owner: liam)
- OPS: add autoscaler hook to drain nodes when fragmentation high (owner: maya)
ops-bot: linked INC-2026-0421 -> task ENG-1234 (ENG-RUNTIME work), ENG-1235 (KV work)
jen: short PR suggestion for runtime env (to test in staging):
```
# set in worker systemd unit
Environment=PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128
Environment=REDWOOD_KV_MAX_BYTES=200000000
```
maya: tested that in staging: fragmentation dropped from ~0.72 -> ~0.38 after ~10m under load. p99 improved ~30%.
liam: great. timeline?
alex: will have metric export PR by EOD tomorrow, then prod rollout the day after if no surprises.
sre-oncall: I'll draft runbook steps and make the alert; include exact promql and remediation steps (evict tenant, reduce context cap, restart worker).
maya: one more note for support: when customers file latency complaints, ask for X-Request-ID and the rough context length. that helps us correlate kv growth.
liam: thanks everyone. we'll track updates on INC-2026-0421. please post follow-ups in this thread. :thumbsup:
